Surfaced by the `os-dev` re-measuring objectui#8345, which reported it as 「noted, not filed」 with **`Carrier: none`** ⇒ the Acceptance-notes fallback does not hold (no named PR or person will touch that line), so it gets a card.

## The claim

`scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs` builds an in-memory strict twin to measure refusals. At **line 284** that twin walks only the **`in`** side of a zod pipe, while the **shipped** walker (`packages/types/src/strict-authoring-face.ts`, via `zod/node-derivation.ts`) walks **both** sides.

⇒ On today's face the two agree exactly (**164 / 571** from either twin, measured with the tolerant face as the lit control at 42 / 571), because no object currently sits on an `out` side. ⚠️ **The first preprocess-wrapped object would be under-reported by the script alone** — and the script is the instrument the consumer-wiring cards (objectui#8346 / #8347) are expected to be judged against.

## Why it is worth a card

It is a **latent divergence between an instrument and the thing it measures**, in the direction where the instrument reads CLEANER than reality. It cannot be caught by the agreement check that exists today, because that check passes precisely while the gap is dormant.

## What triage should settle

Whether the script's twin should be replaced by an import of the shipped `deriveStrictAuthoringSchema` (one instrument instead of two that must be kept in parity), or the pipe arm fixed in place with a pin that reddens if the two twins ever disagree.

Dedupe words: `measure-strict-authoring-face pipe in side only` · `strict twin parity script vs shipped` · `preprocess wrapped object under-reported`
